text:
sara: Hey team — customer ACME reported a big p99 spike on function-calling endpoints after deploy around 06:12 UTC. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~4-6x. Errors are timeouts + 504s sometimes.

mike: Oof. Any obvious rollout tag? which model/route?

sara: Using hosted route `fc-structured-v2` (json-schema validation enabled) and router policy `prefer-low-cost`. Traffic ~5k rps. Degraded after we enabled async tool router change.

tom: Seen similar before when validator added sync validation step for each candidate tool response. Can you attach a sample request/response?

sara: Pasting minimal repro from customer (sanitized):
```json
{
  "input": "fetch_order_status",
  "tools": ["order_api"],
  "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"order_id": {"type": "string"}},
    "required": ["order_id"]
  }
}
```

sara: The agent calls the tool, router waits for validator to parse/validate structured output before returning stream. That validation seems to add ~80-200ms per request under load.

luis: Do we have kernel/serving logs correlating validation CPU? ops-bot can pull p99 by service.

ops-bot: service:router-validator p95=210ms p99=720ms (06:10-06:20 UTC), cpu_avg=78%, queue_depth=12

mike: That's the hotpath. If validator runs synchronously on router main thread it will blow up at scale. We should move schema validation off the critical path (async or background) or use sampling.

tom: Agreed. Short-term mitigation for ACME: disable strict schema validation on their route or switch route to `prefer-latency` which bypasses validator for now. Also can increase validator pool size (config `validator_workers`) if needed.

sara: Customer needs immediate fix. I'm going to create a canary to roll back json-schema validator for ACME and flip to `prefer-latency`. Any objections?

luis: No objections. Also add a rate limit gate for tool-router to reduce queueing.

mike: Steps to reproduce for infra/eng: 1) Run load test 5k rps against fc-structured-v2 with schema validation on. 2) Observe router-validator p99 and overall p99. 3) Swap to schema-disabled and re-run.

tom: Logging tip: capture `router_latency_ms` + `validator_lat_ms` tags per request. Example trace span names: `router.request` -> `tool.call` -> `validator.json_schema`.

sara: I applied temporary config: ACME route -> schema=false, policy=prefer-latency, validator_workers +2 on stage pool. Will monitor.

ops-bot: Deploy event: route-config update for customer ACME by sara at 06:35 UTC.

mike: Please collect a flamegraph for validator thread pool during blast; we need to know whether validation itself is CPU heavy (regexes/complex keywords) or blocking due to I/O.

luis: On it — also checking whether our validator uses `ajv` in strict mode (known to be slower on some schemas). If so, we can use compiled validators and reuse compiled AST per schema id.

tom: Long term ideas: - Move validation to a per-candidate async worker and return best-effort structured output with a validation status flag. - Sample/only-validate N% of responses for high throughput customers. - Cache compiled validators by schema hash. - Add backpressure to tool-router queue when validator latency > threshold.

sara: Customer reports p99 back to normal after change. Will open a follow-up ticket to implement the async-validator change.

mike: Nice. Please include benchmark numbers pre/post and attach load test script. Also add a regression alert rule: if validator_lat_ms_p99 > 500ms then auto-fallback to policy `prefer-latency` for affected routes.

sara: Will do. Creating support ticket 2026-4058 and engineering epic ENG-2123 (async tool-validator).

luis: FYI spotted a minor bug: validator doesn't respect tool timeout header and can hang for long under certain schemas (we should hard-timeout validation at X ms).

tom: Good catch. Add hard timeout + metrics for validation timeouts.

sara: Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes + dashboards. :white_check_mark:
